Fact.Description: One or more sole-proprietor / gig businesses reported on Schedule C. Gross income inclusion authority: 26 U.S.C. § 61.

Fact.Description: Filer finished the Schedule C business loop.

Fact.Name: Had self-employment / gig / freelance income
Fact.Description: Interview gate: whether the filer (or spouse) had self-employment, gig, or freelance income that belongs on Schedule C. Gap evidence Pub 6048 excluded this from upstream Direct File: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p6048.pdf

Fact.Name: Wants qualified business income deduction (no longer asked)
Fact.Description: Kept so saved returns still load. The 26 U.S.C. 199A(a) deduction is not elective (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A), and Form 8995 (form8995.xml, #87) now computes it, so this answer is not used anywhere.

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C QBI deduction case Form 8995 here can't compute
Fact.Description: #87: Schedule C qualified business income is computed on Form 8995 (form8995.xml). This is true when any Form 8995 stop applies: a prior-year loss carryforward, a cooperative patron, active and non-active businesses together, or taxable income before the deduction above the threshold (Form 8995-A). Each part is its own BlockSubmissionOnTrue fact in /flowIsKnockedOut and is complete false without Schedule C income (#186). Used for the Schedule C knockout screen.

Fact.Name: Knockout: the return needs a TY2026 Schedule C, which this tool can't print yet
Fact.Description: #89: true when /hasScheduleCBusinesses is complete and true. A sole proprietor reports the business on Schedule C: Instructions for Schedule C (2025), PDF p. 2 (SHA-256 b5536db91498a450572e37078d7d5ee8fdc400e385d4fee3a26c230a33e399b6), "Use Schedule C (Form 1040) to report income or (loss) from a business you operated or a profession you practiced as a sole proprietor." The 2026 draft Schedule 1, line 3, reads "Business income or (loss). Attach Schedule C", and the 2026 draft Schedule SE, line 2, "Net profit or (loss) from Schedule C, line 31". There is no Schedule C template (2026 draft f1040sc--dft.pdf, SHA-256 287b4510dd847c11f6cbbcc98fee05ac5ff187cc18e1413f8759a4a7cd802224, is not in the repo), so the package would omit it. Complete and false when there is no Schedule C business, so submission checks never see it incomplete. Remove this fact, its /flowIsKnockedOut entry and its PrintRefusingKnockouts entry when the template and field map land.

Fact.Name: Schedule C businesses owned by the secondary filer
Secondary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Sum of /scheduleCBusinesses/*/netProfitOrLoss for the businesses the secondary filer owns: the line 3 of that spouse's own Schedule SE. 2026 draft Instructions for Schedule SE, PDF p. 3: "If both spouses have self-employment income, each must file a separate Schedule SE." $0 on a return that isn't a joint return (only a joint return reports a spouse's business) or when the filer answered no to self-employment income; incomplete while businesses are still being entered, like /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: #118. Every business not owned by the secondary filer is the primary filer's (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/filer defaults to the primary filer), so this is /scheduleCNetProfitOrLoss minus /scheduleCSecondaryFilerNetProfitOrLoss, and the two always add up to Schedule 1 line 3.

Fact.Name: Knockout: spouse-owned Schedule C business
Fact.Description: Schedule SE is figured per filer (scheduleSE /secondaryFilerSelfEmploymentTax, with that spouse's own OASDI base under 26 U.S.C. 1402(b)(1)) and Schedule 2 line 4, Schedule 1 line 15 and Form 8959 line 13 combine both. A secondary filer's business still stops the return until the rest of that spouse's path is per spouse: EITC and CDCC earned income with self-employment (Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 are per spouse), and the printed return has no Schedule SE form yet (one per spouse once it does).

Fact.Name: Knockout: Schedule C cases the EITC, CDCC or ACTC earned income can't yet figure
Fact.Description: #117. The EITC (eitc /eitcEarnedIncomeWithoutCombatPay), the CDCC (income /primaryFilerEarnedIncomeForCdccBase) and the ACTC (income /earnedIncomeWithAllCombatPay) add /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome. Still stopped: - A Schedule C net loss. Both sources say a loss reduces earned income: Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, line 1e and line 4b ("Combine lines 1e, 2c, 3, and 4a"), and the 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5 ("You must reduce your earned income by any loss from self-employment"). /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome is floored at $0, so a loss stops the return when the EITC could apply (AGI below the EITC completed phaseout, eitc /belowEitcAgiLimit, or eitc /eitcQualified), the CDCC applies or the CTC applies. A loss can lower earned income below the EITC limit even when wages alone are above it, so the EITC test is on AGI, which already includes the loss. - A joint return with any Schedule C result and the CDCC: Form 2441 lines 4 and 5 need each spouse's Schedule SE line 3 and Schedule 1 line 15 share ("If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse's earned income separately"), and Schedule SE is not yet figured per spouse. Stopped elsewhere: a spouse-owned business (/flowKnockoutScheduleCSpouseBusiness) and statutory employees (formW2s /flowKnockoutStatutoryEmployee). Church employee income, Forms 4361/4029 and the optional methods have no input in this tool. Complete and false when there is no Schedule C or the Schedule C result is a profit on a return that isn't a joint return claiming the CDCC.

Authority: 26 U.S.C. § 162 (ordinary and necessary expenses paid or incurred in carrying on a trade or business) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/162 Category-level Schedule C Part II lines can replace this bucket in a later PR.

Fact.Name: Net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Schedule C net profit (loss) = gross receipts − expenses. Flows to Schedule 1, line 3 (business income or loss). Gross: § 61; expenses: § 162.

Fact.Name: Schedule C business complete
Fact.Description: Minimum fields for MVP: name, gross receipts, expenses, and (#87) material participation for Form 8995 line 16.

Fact.Name: Filer materially participates in this business
Fact.Description: 26 U.S.C. 199A(i)(2)(B): "The term 'active qualified trade or business' means ... any qualified trade or business of the taxpayer in which the taxpayer materially participates (within the meaning of section 469(h))." 26 U.S.C. 469(h)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/469): material participation means involvement in the operations of the activity "on a basis which is (A) regular, (B) continuous, and (C) substantial." Used for Form 8995 line 16 (minimum deduction).

Fact.Name: Filer does not materially participate in this business
Schedule C businesses with material participation
Schedule C businesses without material participation
Total Schedule C net profit or (loss)
Fact.Description: Sum of Schedule C net profit/(loss) for Schedule 1 line 3 → Form 1040 line 8 (via Schedule 1 line 10). Cite: Schedule C instructions; Form 1040 Schedule 1 line 3.

Fact.Name: Schedule C net profit included in earned income
Fact.Description: Earned income from self-employment for the EITC, CDCC and ACTC = Schedule C net profit (Schedule SE line 3) minus the deductible part of SE tax (Schedule 1 line 15, Schedule SE line 13), 26 U.S.C. 32(c)(2)(A)(ii) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32#c_2_A): "net earnings from self-employment ... determined with regard to the deduction allowed to the taxpayer by section 164(f)". Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), PDF p. 47, EIC Worksheet B, Part 1: "1a. Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 3. ... d. Enter the amount from Schedule SE, Part I, line 13. ... e. Subtract line 1d from line 1c." Under $400 of net earnings no SE tax applies, so this is the Schedule C line 31 net profit (Worksheet B Part 2, line 2b). 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441, PDF p. 5, lines 4 and 5: "2. The amount shown on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 3, minus any deduction you claim on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15." #117: floored at $0 because a loss is not modeled; a loss stops the return wherever it would change a credit (/flowKnockoutScheduleCEarnedIncomeCredits).
